pairs.subject: supply-chain
pairs.evidence: crates/engine-wasm/src/lib.rs:734 In describe_manifest, the host evaluates the untrusted guest module's describe() function to discover its manifest rather than extracting metadata statically or verifying an approved byte digest, deviating from reading-is-not-running where read operations must not execute unapproved code.

techniques.evidence: crates/engine-wasm/src/lib.rs:734 Reading a WASM plugin's self-describing manifest evaluates untrusted guest code via describe.call without static extraction or digest approval.
crates/engine-claude/src/lib.rs:120 ClaudeEngine passes --dangerously-skip-permissions and omits tool restrictions when allowed_tools is empty instead of enforcing least-privilege scoping by default.
crates/engine-wasm/src/lib.rs:526 The WASM host only inspects bare .wasm binary files in the configured directory, never downloading or extracting archive bundles.
crates/engine-wasm/src/lib.rs:738 WASM plugin outputs and manifests are deserialized strictly as structured JSON data, avoiding unsafe object instantiation.

pairs.registryProposal: The reading-is-not-running technique does not distinguish metered in-memory bytecode sandboxes (e.g. wasmtime with CPU fuel and memory ceilings) from unconstrained native/script evaluation; it should clarify whether metered guest manifest probes with zero host imports require digest approval or static metadata sections.
